claims.statement: Polish public procurement creates a large recurring notice stream: the UZP report records about 153,000 contracts awarded under the procurement law in 2024, 130,002 BZP contract or competition notices, and 31,940 Polish contract or competition notices in TED.

SMEs are active participants rather than a merely theoretical customer class: UZP reports that SMEs submitted about 88% of offers below EU thresholds and won about 67% of those procurements in 2024; these aggregates do not identify repeat-bidding SMEs in any particular narrow vertical.

Initial feed access is technically obtainable without a bilateral data deal: TED's search API is anonymous and intended for reuse, while e-Zamowienia says reading BZP notices and statistics does not require its integration procedure.

TED states that procurement notices may generally be reused freely for commercial or noncommercial purposes unless stated otherwise, while attribution and possible third-party or personal-data rights still need to be handled.

The official TED materials establish that this access is nonexclusive: the API documentation explicitly names commercial added-value platforms as users, and the 2025 TED Q&A says many companies already reuse TED data and a private portal may use data identical to TED's.
The official Polish platform is already a free substitute for the lowest-value part of the offer: its terms provide free BZP use, search for proceedings, and daily notice subscriptions.

Direct feature substitutes already exist in Poland: Procuro advertises BZP/TED AI matching and semantic scoring at 110 or 208 PLN per month on annual terms; Och! Przetargi advertises AI SWZ analysis, risk and chance assessment at 150 or 300 PLN per user per month; and PrzetargPro advertises STARTUJ/ROZWAZ/POMIN verdicts and SWZ analysis at 69, 299, or 599 PLN per month. Much of this public pricing is below v1's proposed 499-1,499 PLN monthly range.

Public subscription prices and vendor-hosted customer references support only an inference that organizations pay for tender monitoring and selected-information services; they do not establish that narrow-vertical Polish SMEs will pay 499-1,499 PLN per month for this particular pre-bid gate or renew because of measured bid-cost savings.

Competitors' self-serve, no-card trials and immediate-access sign-up demonstrate a plausible low-friction distribution pattern for tender software, but provide no evidence for v1's own lead cost, trial conversion, sales cycle, partner referral economics, or four-month payback.

No public or candidate-specific evidence establishes fully loaded unit economics for v1, including CAC, trial-to-paid conversion, churn, gross retention, inference and OCR cost per account, document-QA labor, onboarding effort, support burden, professional-liability exposure, contribution margin, or payback.

Bid-preparation cost is real rather than invented: PARP explains that Polish law and case law recognize actually incurred, necessary offer-preparation costs, potentially including documents, bid guarantees, and travel. That source also says the amount depends on the proceeding and must be proved; it does not quantify SME labor wasted on low-fit bids.

There is no candidate-specific evidence that an SME decision owner will trust and act on an automated no-go recommendation, what false-negative rate is tolerable, or whether cited extraction measurably reduces bid labor, missed deadlines, disqualifications, or foregone wins.

Official TED Q&A exposes material data limitations for a reliable gate: unsuccessful tenderers can be omitted, buyer-entered content can contain wrong or missing fields, older and newer formats differ, some procurement documents remain behind practical access restrictions, and some framework or second-stage outcomes lack structured information.

Public-notice reuse is contractible, but the proposed compounding asset is only partially under founder control: public notices and awards do not by themselves contain a client's no-bid decisions, internal margin, preparation effort, or reasons. Those outcome labels could become proprietary only through explicit customer agreements and repeated collection.

No evidence establishes signed customer consent, data-processing and reuse terms, portability and retention rights, a reliable outcome-labeling workflow, or enough recurring paid accounts to create the claimed permissioned outcome dataset.

Although the founder can own independently written code and direct subscriptions, v1's presently evidenced mechanism is replaceable rather than a durable control point: official inputs are open to competitors, free official search and alerts exist, and multiple vendors already market overlapping scoring and go/no-go features. A defensible permissioned outcome asset is not yet contracted or demonstrated.

The founder's family-business access may make a renewable-installation pilot reachable, but there is no evidence that this company repeatedly bids, suffers the claimed avoidable bid loss, will adopt a machine recommendation, or grants reusable outcome-data rights.

The national aggregates do not establish the minimum viable vertical: no selected CPV niche has evidence here for qualified-notice frequency, addressable repeat bidders, average preparation hours, disqualification or abandonment rate, recoverable loss per decision, or willingness to pay.

contrary_evidence: Official e-Zamowienia search and daily subscriptions are free, so basic discovery and alerting cannot justify the proposed price.
At least three current Polish products publicly advertise overlapping AI matching, SWZ analysis, risk assessment, or explicit go/no-go verdicts, commonly at prices below v1's hypothesis.
TED explicitly permits commercial reuse and says many companies already do it; an entrant can use data identical to TED's, so public-feed access is not scarce.

Official TED workshops document missing outcome fields, optional unsuccessful-bidder data, buyer-entered errors, schema evolution, and practical document-access restrictions that can break confident automation.
The research found no direct proof of v1 paid adoption, decision use, recurring retention, CAC/payback, or a contracted permissioned outcome-data asset.

unknowns: Which narrow technical vertical has enough qualified notices and repeat-bidding SMEs to support recurring paid volume.
The actual fully loaded labor and external cost of a bid, the fraction wasted on detectably bad-fit tenders, and the recoverable loss per screened decision.
Whether the target sales owner will pay 499-1,499 PLN monthly after comparing free official tools and lower-priced AI competitors.
Paid-pilot conversion, monthly and annual renewal, churn, expansion, CAC, sales-cycle length, partner commission, contribution margin, and cash payback.
The acceptable false-negative rate and whether users will follow a no-go recommendation when a missed public contract has material upside.
The accuracy and reviewer time required to extract eligibility, geography, deadline, margin inputs, and contractual risk across Polish and EU document formats.
The customer contract and consent language needed to retain, aggregate, derive features from, and reuse bid/no-bid, effort, margin, submission, and outcome labels.
The number and duration of paid accounts required before outcome labels improve vertical calibration beyond what an incumbent or frontier model can reproduce.
Whether the founder's family renewable-energy company is a frequent bidder, has the claimed loss, and is willing to serve as a permissioned design partner.
The support, procurement-law review, security, incident-response, and professional-liability burden compatible with a five-hour-per-day founder limit.
